Job Description

Job Overview

The Operations Director will be responsible for directing and implementing company policy to ensure compliance with contract responsibilities.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Executive Director Opportunity Profile & Job Description
Impact46 | Lawrenceville, Georgia

Lead. Connect. Build. Serve.

Help shape the next chapter of Impact46—and the community it serves.

About Impact46 Impact46 strengthens Lawrenceville by bringing people, organizations, and resources together to improve quality of life and community well-being. Working at the intersection of city government, the faith community, and the broader community, we identify needs, build partnerships, and turn collaboration into practical service. Current initiatives include City-supported utility and housing assistance; shelter and development services for men experiencing homelessness; leadership development for high school students; a summer internship program; and other programs designed to strengthen both citizens and the Lawrenceville community.

The Opportunity Impact46 has established strong programs, trusted partnerships, and meaningful community support. The Board, City leaders, faith community, and community partners are committed to its continued success. We are seeking an Executive Director who can build on that tradition of service to lead Impact46 into its next chapter. The right leader will combine vision with execution—recognizing emerging needs, developing distinctive services and partnerships, expanding financial support, leading staff effectively, and ensuring that Impact46 remains accountable, well-managed, and focused on measurable community impact.

What the Executive Director Will Lead Strategic direction
—working with the Board to turn Lawrenceville needs and opportunities into focused priorities and measurable results.
Fundraising and development
—building relationships with donors, churches, businesses, foundations, and grant makers to diversify and grow financial support.
Community partnerships
—strengthening Impact46's relationships with the City of Lawrenceville, faith community, schools, nonprofits, civic organizations, businesses, and community leaders.
Organizational leadership
—leading the Operations Director, Program Director, and staff through clear expectations, accountability, strong systems, and a culture of service and excellence.
Program impact
—ensuring current programs remain effective while developing thoughtful new initiatives that fit Impact46's mission and capacity.
Financial stewardship and Board partnership
—maintaining organizational sustainability, transparency, and a productive relationship with the volunteer Board of Directors.

The Leader We Are Looking For We are looking for a visible, trusted, and entrepreneurial community leader who can move comfortably among city leaders, pastors, donors, business leaders, staff, students, volunteers, and the people Impact46 serves.
A relationship-builder who earns trust and brings people with different perspectives together around a common purpose.
A successful fundraiser who is comfortable inviting people and organizations to invest in a mission that matters.
A strategic thinker who sees possibilities and can turn good ideas into practical, sustainable action.
A strong manager who develops people, establishes accountability, and leads without controlling every detail.
A compelling communicator who can clearly tell the Impact46 story and demonstrate its value to Lawrenceville.
A leader who combines compassion with accountability, innovation with responsible stewardship, and vision with sound judgment and integrity.

What Success Looks Like Success will be reflected in a stronger and more sustainable Impact46: expanded and diversified financial support, deeper community partnerships, effective staff leadership, measurable program results, thoughtful new initiatives, and a reputation for integrity, collaboration, and meaningful service to Lawrenceville.

Position Summary & Core Responsibilities The Executive Director (ED) is the chief executive officer of Impact46 and is accountable to the Board of Directors for strategy, fundraising, community relationships, staff leadership, financial stewardship, and organizational performance. The ED advances Impact46's mission by working closely with city government, the faith community, businesses, schools, nonprofits, donors, and other community partners. The ED directly supervises the Operations Director and Program Director.

Strategic Leadership & Community Impact

Implement Board-approved strategy and convert priorities into measurable annual goals.
Identify emerging Lawrenceville needs and develop appropriate programs, partnerships, and funding strategies.
Evaluate programs for mission alignment, measurable results, cost effectiveness, and continued community need.
Negotiate and administer contracts and intergovernmental agreements for Impact46 and its points of service.
Report organizational performance, opportunities, and significant risks to the Board.

Fundraising & Development

Own and execute the annual fundraising and development plan with measurable revenue goals.
Personally cultivate, solicit, and steward major donors, churches, businesses, foundations, and other funding partners.
Lead grant prospecting, proposal development, renewals, reporting, and foundation relationships.
Diversify contributed revenue through individual giving, corporate support, sponsorships, church support, grants, campaigns, and events.
Engage Board members in donor introductions, cultivation, fundraising, and stewardship; report fundraising performance regularly.

City, Faith & Community Relations

Serve as Impact46's principal public representative and maintain a visible, trusted presence in Lawrenceville.
Maintain strong working relationships with the City of Lawrenceville, elected officials, city staff, faith leaders, businesses, schools, civic organizations, foundations, nonprofits, and volunteers.
Coordinate with the City and community stakeholders on the Mayor's Quarterly Faith Luncheon and monthly Community Prayer Gatherings.
Communicate Impact46's mission, results, needs, and vision clearly to partners, supporters, media, and the community.

Staff & Organizational Management

Directly supervise, develop, and evaluate the Operations Director, Program Director, and other senior staff as assigned.
Set clear goals, responsibilities, performance expectations, and accountability for senior leadership.
Ensure effective personnel policies, management systems, organizational procedures, and internal communication.
Recruit and retain qualified staff and maintain a culture of service, integrity, teamwork, accountability, and excellence.
Address significant personnel and organizational issues promptly and appropriately.

Program Oversight

Hold the Program Director accountable for program delivery, quality, outcomes, and compliance with funding commitments.
Ensure programs remain responsive to community needs and consistent with Impact46's mission and strategy.
Use program data and outcomes to guide decisions, demonstrate impact, and support fundraising and community engagement.

Financial Stewardship

Develop the annual operating budget with staff and Board leadership and recommend it for Board approval.
Monitor revenue, expenses, cash flow, restricted funds, fundraising performance, and overall financial condition.
Ensure appropriate financial controls, accurate reporting, required filings, audits or reviews, and grant compliance.
Identify financial risks early and strengthen reserves and long-term sustainability.

Board Partnership & Governance

Maintain a candid, professional, and productive relationship with the Board and provide timely information for effective governance and decision-making.
Work with the Board Chair to prepare effective meetings and implement Board-approved policies and direction.
Support Board recruitment, orientation, engagement, fundraising, and community ambassadorship.
Maintain clear boundaries between Board governance and executive management. The ED reports to the Board collectively.

Experience & Qualifications Candidates should bring significant leadership experience in a nonprofit, faith-based, community, governmental, business, or related organization; demonstrated success in fundraising, donor or grant development, and community relationship-building; experience leading professional staff and working with a volunteer Board; and strong strategic, financial, organizational, and communication skills. Sound judgment, integrity, discretion, professionalism, and commitment to Impact46's mission and faith-based service philosophy are required. A bachelor's degree is required; an advanced degree in a related area is preferred.

The Questions That Guide Our Work What does Lawrenceville need?
What can Impact46 uniquely do about it?
Who can we bring together to make it happen?
How will we sustain it—and how will we know we made a difference?

Impact46 is ready for its next chapter. We are looking for the leader who is ready to help write it.

Position Details & Application Process Reports To:
Impact46 Board of Directors
Directly Supervises:
Operations Director, Program Director, and other senior staff as assigned
Primary External Relationships:
City of Lawrenceville; faith community; donors and foundations; businesses; schools; civic and nonprofit organizations; volunteers; and community leaders
Compensation:
$100,000 – $125,000 annually + benefits
Work Location:
Lawrenceville, GA (Hybrid: 4 days in office / 1 day remote each week)

To Apply:
Submit your Resume and Cover Letter by October 13, 2026
to adam@impact46.org
.

jobs.description:
Are you excellent at managing teams, engaging stakeholders, building relationships, and managing multiple projects and priorities? Are you exceptionally strategic and stay calm under pressure? If this perfectly describes you, there might be a spot for you on our client’s team.

Our client, a leading not-for-profit organization in the Innovation and Technology sector based in Lagos, is looking to fill the position of Executive Director. With members spread across Nigeria, the organization supports a community of over 150 innovation and technology hubs, fostering policy advocacy, creating linkages, and promoting sustainability. They also facilitate capacity building through knowledge-sharing events, demo days, and meet-the-funders sessions.

The Executive Director will report to the Board of Directors and be responsible for providing overall leadership and overseeing the organization’s day-to-day operations. The successful candidate will drive the organization’s programs, ensure the achievement of strategic priorities, and contribute to the organization’s vision.

Key Responsibilities

The Executive Director will be responsible for the following:

Overseeing the organization’s day-to-day operations, developing and implementing strategies to achieve the organization’s mission and goals.
Leading and managing the secretariat team and resources, ensuring optimal performance and results.
Representing the organization externally and building relationships with stakeholders, partners, and funders.
Planning and executing projects to create a cohesive ecosystem experience for members.
Acting as the main point of contact for the ecosystem, providing support and addressing stakeholder queries.
Ensuring adherence to corporate governance and regulatory compliance requirements.
Initiating, executing, and supporting fundraising and partnership initiatives, including grant management and reporting.
Driving business development by identifying opportunities and developing partnership initiatives, programs, and policy proposals.
Strengthening connections, knowledge management, and information exchange within the ecosystem.
Organizing workshops, meetings, and events with sectorial and industry stakeholders to support the organization’s mission.
Developing and managing the organization’s annual budget and programs.
Preparing financial reports and maintaining financial records.
Implementing talent sourcing, management, and development strategies and processes.
Tracking and reporting the organization’s performance and evaluating impact to drive sustainability.

Skills & Experience

Proven leadership skills.
Business acumen and stakeholder engagement.
Strategic thinking and effective communication skills.
Ability to manage teams for results and make informed decisions.
Resilience, adaptability, and resourcefulness.
Attention to detail and ability to manage multiple projects.
Innovation and entrepreneurial mindset.
Networking and relationship building.
Fundraising and resource mobilization experience.
Community engagement, advocacy, and collaboration skills.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree

jobs.title: Senior Director of Development, Engineering
jobs.description:
Case Western Reserve University is committed to providing a transparent estimate of the salary range available for this position at the time of its posting. The salary range is between $89,491 and $113,207, depending on qualifications, experience, department budgets, and industry data.

Employees receive more than just a paycheck. University employees enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare, retirement plans, tuition assistance, paid time off, and a winter recess.

POSITION OBJECTIVE

The senior director of development will initiate, cultivate, develop and maintain a comprehensive development program. The senior director envisions and implements strategies necessary to meet Case School of Engineering and Case Western Reserve University driven goals surpassing $33 million annually. As a member of the senior development team the senior director will provide concepts, leadership, insights, tactics and execution of the engineering school development plan. In addition to and in coordination with the vice dean, the senior director is responsible for the development of overall fundraising plans for the school and the university. Functioning as part of the university-wide development team and working closely with the vice dean, the vice president for school and college development, and the dean, the senior director will be expected to work collegially, and in partnership with school-based colleagues and also must develop a strong relationship with central development personnel, university trustees and the president and provost. This person will engage in direct face-to-face cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of donors and participate in planning and implementing school-specific initiatives.

Essential Functions

Identify, cultivate, solicit and steward major gifts ($500,000 to $1,000,000) for the school in accordance with fundraising priorities established by the dean and vice dean. Travel to meet face-to-face with prospects and donors. Plan and execute gift strategies in conjunction with all central and school based external relations team at the university (30%)
Partner with the vice dean in developing and implementing a comprehensive fundraising strategy for the Case School of Engineering, including campaign planning, principal and major gift strategy, prospect pipeline development, staff and volunteer leadership, and fundraising priorities. (20%)
Cultivate and solicit major gift prospects, primarily from the engineering school and globally based alumni. (10%)
Serve as primary development staff contact for associate deans, department chairs, institutes, events, donors and other senior faculty. Work with departments and institutes in the planning and implementation of department and interdepartmental fundraising efforts with specific emphasis on the global market. Serve as development liaison to the office of international affairs and host foreign dignitaries, parents of current students and international institutions. (10%)
Collaborate with faculty and academic leaders to identify and develop philanthropic opportunities that advance the Case School of Engineering¿s academic, research and student priorities. Identify, cultivate and develop strategic relationships with corporations, foundations, alumni, donors and other external partners whose interests align with the school's priorities. Connect external stakeholders with faculty, staff and students to strengthen engagement, advance the school's mission and generate significant philanthropic investment. (15%)
Recruit, train and manage volunteers of the alumni development cabinet and think tanks and other committees as appropriate, who will actively participate in the rating, cultivating, and soliciting of major gift prospects across the globe. (7.5%)
Supervise a team of national development gift officers and serve as mentor to external relations team. (7.5%)

Nonessential Functions

Perform other duties assigned by the vice dean and dean, including but not limited to management of other existing and future development, alumni programs. (<1%)

CONTACTS

Department: Frequent contact with dean, vice president, vice/associate deans, department chairs and directors. Contact with faculty, students and staff as required to perform essential functions.

University: Develop and coordinate strategy with a wide range of partners: the president's office, provost, vice presidents, deans, trustees, alumni, directors of administrative departments, faculty and staff.

External: Daily contact with donors, alumni, foundation representatives, community organizers/advocates, corporate executives and federal and foreign government officials. Contact with foreign visitors and officials and academic boards and organizations as required to perform essential functions.

Students: Contact with undergraduate, graduate and professional students as required to perform essential functions.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY

Direct supervisory responsibility for three directors of national development.

Qualifications

Experience: 10 or more years of experience in development or related field. Experience in the fields of higher education preferred. Experience with international travel and international alumni engagement.

Education: Bachelor's degree is required. Master's degree preferred.

Required Skills

Oversight and management of discussion and negotiation of agreements between educational institutions.
Goal oriented with a high level of energy, enthusiasm and dedication to the mission and goals of the Case School of Engineering and Case Western Reserve University.
Must be able to work with and command the confidence of donors, their financial and legal advisors as well as senior officers of the university.
Demonstrated front-line fundraising experience at the leadership gift level.
Must be able to work both independently and collaboratively with colleagues. Ability to interact with colleagues, supervisors, and customers face to face.
Ability to maintain database of cultural, educational and governmental agencies with international ties.
Computer proficiency (including Microsoft Office) and the ability to learn new programs.
Ability to meet consistent attendance.
Ability to demonstrate history of successful support, education, and advocacy for all students, aligned with the values, mission, and messaging of the university, while adhering to the staff policy on conflict of commitment and interest.
Willingness to learn and work with artificial intelligence (AI) tools and technologies.

WORKING CONDITIONS

General office environment, some evening and weekend work hours will be required. Frequent travel required.

This position is eligible for hybrid work arrangement up to two remote days per week at the discretion of the department. New employees may begin a hybrid schedule upon approval from the supervisor, successful completion of an orientation period and signing the remote work checklist certification form.

Case Western Reserve University is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants are protected under federal and state laws and university policy from discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national or ethnic origin, protected veteran status, disability, age and genetic information.

Case Western Reserve University complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act regarding reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application and hiring process should contact the CWRU Office of Equity at 216-368-3066 to request a reasonable accommodation. Determinations as to granting reasonable accommodations for any applicants will be made on a case-by-case basis.

new_jobs.title: Senior Director of Development, Engineering
new_jobs.description:
Case Western Reserve University is committed to providing a transparent estimate of the salary range available for this position at the time of its posting. The salary range is between $89,491 and $113,207, depending on qualifications, experience, department budgets, and industry data.

Employees receive more than just a paycheck. University employees enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare, retirement plans, tuition assistance, paid time off, and a winter recess.

POSITION OBJECTIVE

The senior director of development will initiate, cultivate, develop and maintain a comprehensive development program. The senior director envisions and implements strategies necessary to meet Case School of Engineering and Case Western Reserve University driven goals surpassing $33 million annually. As a member of the senior development team the senior director will provide concepts, leadership, insights, tactics and execution of the engineering school development plan. In addition to and in coordination with the vice dean, the senior director is responsible for the development of overall fundraising plans for the school and the university. Functioning as part of the university-wide development team and working closely with the vice dean, the vice president for school and college development, and the dean, the senior director will be expected to work collegially, and in partnership with school-based colleagues and also must develop a strong relationship with central development personnel, university trustees and the president and provost. This person will engage in direct face-to-face cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of donors and participate in planning and implementing school-specific initiatives.

Essential Functions

Identify, cultivate, solicit and steward major gifts ($500,000 to $1,000,000) for the school in accordance with fundraising priorities established by the dean and vice dean. Travel to meet face-to-face with prospects and donors. Plan and execute gift strategies in conjunction with all central and school based external relations team at the university (30%)
Partner with the vice dean in developing and implementing a comprehensive fundraising strategy for the Case School of Engineering, including campaign planning, principal and major gift strategy, prospect pipeline development, staff and volunteer leadership, and fundraising priorities. (20%)
Cultivate and solicit major gift prospects, primarily from the engineering school and globally based alumni. (10%)
Serve as primary development staff contact for associate deans, department chairs, institutes, events, donors and other senior faculty. Work with departments and institutes in the planning and implementation of department and interdepartmental fundraising efforts with specific emphasis on the global market. Serve as development liaison to the office of international affairs and host foreign dignitaries, parents of current students and international institutions. (10%)
Collaborate with faculty and academic leaders to identify and develop philanthropic opportunities that advance the Case School of Engineering¿s academic, research and student priorities. Identify, cultivate and develop strategic relationships with corporations, foundations, alumni, donors and other external partners whose interests align with the school's priorities. Connect external stakeholders with faculty, staff and students to strengthen engagement, advance the school's mission and generate significant philanthropic investment. (15%)
Recruit, train and manage volunteers of the alumni development cabinet and think tanks and other committees as appropriate, who will actively participate in the rating, cultivating, and soliciting of major gift prospects across the globe. (7.5%)
Supervise a team of national development gift officers and serve as mentor to external relations team. (7.5%)

Nonessential Functions

Perform other duties assigned by the vice dean and dean, including but not limited to management of other existing and future development, alumni programs. (<1%)

CONTACTS

Department: Frequent contact with dean, vice president, vice/associate deans, department chairs and directors. Contact with faculty, students and staff as required to perform essential functions.

University: Develop and coordinate strategy with a wide range of partners: the president's office, provost, vice presidents, deans, trustees, alumni, directors of administrative departments, faculty and staff.

External: Daily contact with donors, alumni, foundation representatives, community organizers/advocates, corporate executives and federal and foreign government officials. Contact with foreign visitors and officials and academic boards and organizations as required to perform essential functions.

Students: Contact with undergraduate, graduate and professional students as required to perform essential functions.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY

Direct supervisory responsibility for three directors of national development.

Qualifications

Experience: 10 or more years of experience in development or related field. Experience in the fields of higher education preferred. Experience with international travel and international alumni engagement.

Education: Bachelor's degree is required. Master's degree preferred.

Required Skills

Oversight and management of discussion and negotiation of agreements between educational institutions.
Goal oriented with a high level of energy, enthusiasm and dedication to the mission and goals of the Case School of Engineering and Case Western Reserve University.
Must be able to work with and command the confidence of donors, their financial and legal advisors as well as senior officers of the university.
Demonstrated front-line fundraising experience at the leadership gift level.
Must be able to work both independently and collaboratively with colleagues. Ability to interact with colleagues, supervisors, and customers face to face.
Ability to maintain database of cultural, educational and governmental agencies with international ties.
Computer proficiency (including Microsoft Office) and the ability to learn new programs.
Ability to meet consistent attendance.
Ability to demonstrate history of successful support, education, and advocacy for all students, aligned with the values, mission, and messaging of the university, while adhering to the staff policy on conflict of commitment and interest.
Willingness to learn and work with artificial intelligence (AI) tools and technologies.

WORKING CONDITIONS

General office environment, some evening and weekend work hours will be required. Frequent travel required.

This position is eligible for hybrid work arrangement up to two remote days per week at the discretion of the department. New employees may begin a hybrid schedule upon approval from the supervisor, successful completion of an orientation period and signing the remote work checklist certification form.

Case Western Reserve University complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act regarding reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application and hiring process should contact the CWRU Office of Equity at 216-368-3066 to request a reasonable accommodation. Determinations as to granting reasonable accommodations for any applicants will be made on a case-by-case basis.
